title: Removing a regular point to arrange infinity
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a punctually pure lisse Weil sheaf of weight $w$
on a dense open $U_0\subset\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$.
After a finite constant-field extension, there are a dense open
$V_0\subset\mathbf A^1$ and a lisse sheaf $\mathcal E$ on $V_0$
of the same weight, with trivial local inertia at infinity, together
with a Frobenius-equivariant surjection

$$
H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal F).
$$

Geometric irreducibility is preserved.

proof.text: Choose a finite extension with a regular rational point. Use the finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Since the nonempty open $U_0$ in $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x]$ contains a nonempty basic open $D(f)$ for some nonzero $f\in k_0[x]$, choose $m\geq1$ with $q^m>\deg f$. A nonzero polynomial has at most its degree many roots, so some $a\in k'_0=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$ has $f(a)\ne0$. Thus $s_0=(x=a)$ is a $k'_0$-rational point of $U'_0:=U_0\times_{k_0}k'_0$. Set $W_0=U'_0\setminus\{s_0\}$. This is still a dense nonempty open: deleting one closed point from an open of the integral affine line does not delete its generic point. The common geometric fibre of $U'_0$ and $U_0$ is $U$.

source.place: first paragraph, choice of s over a finite extension

proof.text: Regard $\mathcal F$ on $U$ with its $k'_0$-Weil structure $\theta^{[m]}=\theta\circ g_U^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ(g_U^{m-1})^*\theta$, using [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]; denote this sheaf by $\mathcal F'$. Its underlying lisse sheaf is unchanged. If $y$ is a closed point of $U'_0$ above $x\in U_0$, put $e=[\kappa(y):\kappa(x)]$. The residue-field Frobenius over $\kappa(y)$ is the $e$-th power of that over $\kappa(x)$; the iterated-stalk definition [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] therefore makes its stalk operator $F_x^e$ (up to the choice of the geometric lift). Triangularizing $F_x$ shows that its eigenvalues become $\alpha^e$, and $q_y=q_x^e$. Thus $|\iota(\alpha^e)|=q_x^{ew/2}=q_y^{w/2}$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. This verifies punctual purity of weight $w$ after the constant extension, including nonsemisimple stalk operators.

source.place: first paragraph, preservation of the local weight condition under the finite extension

proof.text: Use homogeneous coordinates $[X:Z]$ on $\mathbf P^1_{k'_0}$ and set $\tau[X:Z]=[Z:X-aZ]$. Its matrix has determinant $-1$, and its inverse is $[Y:T]\mapsto[aY+T:Y]$; these formulas work in characteristic two as well. Hence $\tau$ is a $k'_0$-isomorphism, sends $s_0=[a:1]$ to $\infty=[1:0]$, and is $x\mapsto1/(x-a)$ away from $s_0$. Define $V_0=\tau(W_0)\subset\mathbf A^1_{k'_0}$ and $h=\tau|_{W_0}:W_0\xrightarrow{\sim}V_0$. Define $\mathcal E=(h^{-1})^*(\mathcal F'|_{W_0})$. Transport of the local constant systems of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] makes $\mathcal E$ lisse. Since $h$ is defined over $k'_0$, its pullback commutes with the geometric Frobenius and transports the Weil isomorphism of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Stalks, residue fields and their local operators are identified under $h$, so purity follows directly from [def-weil-punctual-weights]. More strongly, $(\tau^{-1})^*\mathcal F'$ is lisse on $\tau(U'_0)=V_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and restricts to $\mathcal E$. By the extension criterion in [rem-dl-a1-conventions], $\mathcal E$ is unramified at infinity. Thus no ramification hypothesis on the original infinity was used.

source.place: first paragraph, the projective coordinate change and lisse extension across the new infinity

proof.text: Suppose the original underlying geometric sheaf $\mathcal F$ is irreducible. The geometric curve $U$ is a nonempty open of $\mathbf A^1_k$, hence connected, normal and Noetherian; the geometric $W=U\setminus\{s\}$ is nonempty and dense. Apply the geometric-sheaf clause of part (4) of [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective] to $W\hookrightarrow U$: $\mathcal F|_W$ is irreducible. Equivalently part (1) says that $\pi_1(W)\to\pi_1(U)$ is surjective, so no new invariant subspace can occur on restriction. Constant-field extension did not change $U$ or its underlying geometric sheaf, and the isomorphism $h$ induces inverse equivalences of their sheaf categories. Therefore $\mathcal E$ is geometrically irreducible. This assertion concerns geometric irreducibility only; arithmetic irreducibility need not survive a constant-field extension.

source.place: first paragraph, restriction to a dense open preserves geometric irreducibility

proof.text:
Let $j_0:W_0\hookrightarrow U'_0$ and $i_0:s_0\hookrightarrow U'_0$ be the complementary immersions. All schemes are separated and of finite type over $k'_0$, and $\ell$ is invertible. For the constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F'$ in degree zero, [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] supplies the localization triangle with all arrows Weil-equivariant. Apply the localization-under-$Rf_!$ clause of [prop-functor-package] with $f:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives the triangle with terms $R\Gamma_c(W,\mathcal F'|_W)$, $R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal F')$, $R\Gamma_c(s,\mathcal F'_s)$, after the point-fibre interpretation of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Work on the underlying coefficient complexes, not in a purported derived category of Weil sheaves. By [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] the point-fibre functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is an exact equivalence (it commutes with shifts and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles) onto the finite-dimensional derived category over the coefficient field, so the triangle becomes a distinguished triangle of coefficient complexes. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], applied at a common finite coefficient-field stage and then extended to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, has the exact segment
$$H_c^1(W,\mathcal F'|_W)\longrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal F')\longrightarrow H_c^1(s,\mathcal F'_s).$$
Exact coefficient-field transport and the equivariance of these comparisons are clauses of [prop-functor-package]. Thus both displayed arrows commute with Frobenius over $k'_0$.

source.place: second paragraph, recollement followed by compact-support direct image and its degree-one exact sequence

proof.text:
The closed scheme $s_0=\operatorname{Spec}k'_0$ is finite over the current constant field, and $\mathcal F'_s$ is constructible. At $r=1$, [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology-positive] makes the last term of the preceding segment zero, in the cohomology convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Exactness then makes its first arrow surjective. Finally $h:W\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ has $h_*\mathcal F'|_W=\mathcal E$ by its definition as transport of a sheaf. Direct image along an isomorphism is the inverse equivalence to pullback and is exact; $h$ is proper, so the proper-coincidence and compact-support-composition clauses of [prop-functor-package] identify $R\Gamma_c(V,\mathcal E)$ with $R\Gamma_c(W,\mathcal F'|_W)$. Composing this identification on $H^1$ with the surjection constructs
$$H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal F).$$
The schemes and $h$ are defined over $k'_0$, and every comparison used here is Weil-equivariant by [prop-functor-package]. The underlying geometric sheaf on the right is the original $\mathcal F$; its Weil operator is the iterate over $k'_0$ used in step 2. Thus this is precisely a Frobenius-equivariant surjection after the asserted finite constant-field extension.

source.place: second paragraph, point vanishing, surjectivity and transport by tau
